title: XGBoost on multimodal MRI identifies depression in cerebral small vessel disease
summary: A retrospective three-centre study of 198 participants built models from structural, functional and diffusion tensor MRI features with nine classifiers. An XGBoost model on 12 features reached AUCs of 0.958 (training, n=113), 0.893 (external cohort 1, n=85) and 0.917 (external cohort 2, n=102). SHAP analysis pointed to higher low-frequency fluctuation amplitude in the superior frontal gyrus and lower fractional anisotropy in the default mode network. The cohorts are small and the study is retrospective.
ai_technology: XGBoost classifier (best of nine) on 12 multimodal MRI features
organization: Wenzhou Medical University; Lishui Central Hospital

evidence.tested: Two external validation cohorts (n=85, n=102): AUC 0.893 and 0.917.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective, small cohorts; clinical use untested; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: XGBoost selected and combined MRI features to separate patients with and without depression.
